name: igp-migration-t1-2node
description: 2-node Arista cEOS lab running OSPF area 0 (brownfield baseline). The program migrates its IGP to IS-IS in four gated phases; each phase's package is human-applied out-of-band and the next phase re-harvests the applied live state.

nodes.name: ceos1
nodes.role: one end of the single point-to-point IGP link; both devices carry the full migration

nodes.name: ceos2
nodes.role: one end of the single point-to-point IGP link; both devices carry the full migration

links.routing: ospf 1, area 0.0.0.0, network point-to-point, ip ospf cost 10 (both ends)

_note: The brownfield state the migration starts from. Static facts here are the authored rig
baseline; anything created DURING the program (applied phase state) is declared runtime
below and is discoverable only by harvesting the live devices after each gate's apply.
igpBaseline.protocol: ospf, process 1, single area 0.0.0.0 on every IGP interface
igpBaseline.costIntent: explicit per-interface ip ospf cost (10, both ends of the single link) — the metric intent the IS-IS translation must carry forward
igpBaseline.bgp: NONE — this network runs no BGP; the IGP is the only routing protocol
igpBaseline.targetProtocolPresence: IS-IS does NOT exist on any device at program start — P1's harvest finds none and CREATE is the expected outcome
igpBaseline.appliedPhaseState: RUNTIME — the live state after each gate's human apply (adjacencies formed, route sets, preference in effect). Re-harvested by each leg; never knowable from this file
igpBaseline._whyThisIsUnarguablyRuntime: Applied phase state is created out-of-band by a human operator DURING the program, between legs. It does not exist when the Program Architect runs, changes at every gate, and can differ from intent (an apply can fail or partially take) — so it cannot be pinned in a static artifact or an interface contract, and must be read from the live devices each time.
igpBaseline._topologyNote: TWO nodes, ONE link. A 3-node triangle (with a transit-path preference to preserve) was authored but SHELVED: it does not fit the prod host, and cEOS does not boot on the available off-host VM. The four-phase migration story is unaffected; only the transit-path narrative is absent.

interdependency.dag: plan-gate -> P1 (coexistence deploy) -> G1 (human apply) -> P2 (parity evidence) -> G2 (accept evidence) -> P3 (preference shift) -> G3 (human apply) -> P4 (OSPF removal) -> final gate (human apply)
interdependency.chainedValue: each leg's report (declared applied values + findings); the TRUTH of applied state rides the re-harvest, not the edge — legs compare the two
interdependency.direction_note: Every leg consumes the interface contract's constants (NETs, metrics, preference mechanism) as designed by the plan — legs restate them and are forbidden from re-deriving them. Each leg additionally consumes its predecessor's report via the DAG edge, and must verify the predecessor's declared applied state against its own live harvest rather than trusting either alone.
